chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Fourteen [Gre
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Fourteen Great States of Divine Wisdom

---

**¶1:**
What are the fourteen principal states of divine wisdom proceeding from the Lord?

---

**¶3:**
The [GAP-1] states that subsist below abide in fourteen [GAP-2] degrees of divine wisdom: the five essential faculties of spiritual perception — the truths born from the Lord's divine rational — together with the influx of divine truth and its reception in the understanding. These communicate good into those faculties, dwelling within them as life itself. Together they constitute a holy fullness: five interior faculties united with the two principles of divine communication and reception.

---

**¶4:**
[GAP-3] The five truths proceeding from the Lord's operative divine life, which [GAP-4: sustain and uphold] the entire burden of spiritual order; together with the Lord's operative life [and the divine rational], the origins from which they proceed. [GAP-5] These are the principles through which all spiritual order is constituted and maintained.

---

**¶5:**
There are fourteen states of divine wisdom [GAP-6] [GAP-7] — the interior ground of the will that has not yet been made manifest. This ground of reception [GAP-8] is made firm and established. These states endured against the assault of evil and falsity [GAP-9] nothing from the opposition is their equal. The hidden fullness of divine good that [GAP-10] — the divine truth sent forth from divine love, the [GAP-11] — this truth came and established itself immovably at the center of all these states [GAP-12]: he is recognized as the benevolent origin of good for [GAP-13: all] the states of wisdom and all spiritual powers that are holy and conjoined in unity. He has become sovereign governor and supreme ruling truth after the likeness of divine love itself, the lord over all workings of divine providence. The whole of spiritual order coheres through their united purpose [GAP-14] unto the consummation of all states.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: what are the [f]ourteen grea[t a]eons of light?

the [gods of light] below abide in fourteen [great aeons of light]: the five elements, the sons of the First Man, together with the call and the hearing. They anoint them, living in them. These shall make seven, five plus two.

[Also the] f[ive s]ons of the Living Spirit who [support] all [the wei]ght of the universe; together with the [Li]vi[ng] Spirit [and the Fir]st Man, their fathers. [These also are seven] by which the universe is established.

[There are fourt]een aeons of light [that abide] [within the la]nd that is not revealed. This land [in which all the aeons abide is made firm and is estab]lished. They bore up under the enemy [and they were not overcome for no one of the darkness equa]ls them. The hidden plenitude that [abides in] the Ambassador who came from the Father, the [great luminary] He came and stood firm in the midst of these [aeons of light]: he is called the good father of [all] the ae[ons and gods] who are holy and conjoined. He has become leader and a great king after the likeness of the first Father, the lord of all these cou[nse]ls. This universe is held together by their will [from the beginning] to the end of all things.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading's "states that subsist below" corresponds in the Kephalaia's register to "gods of light" — the collective divine entities active in the lower cosmos, consistent with the later pairing "aeons and gods" in ¶5.
Completes the phrase to match the chapter title "the fourteen great aeons of light," corresponding to the spiritual reading's "degrees of divine wisdom."
Standard Kephalaia transitional phrase introducing the second group of seven, parallel to the enumeration of the first seven in ¶3.

The editor's "support" is confirmed: the five sons of the Living Spirit are universally described in Manichaean cosmology as supporting/upholding the weight of the universe, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "sustain and uphold."

Parallel counting statement matching ¶3's "These shall make seven, five plus two" — here five sons plus the Living Spirit and the First Man also make seven, the principles through which the universe is established.

Natural connector describing the fourteen aeons' dwelling, linking them to the hidden land described in GAP-7; "abide" is characteristic Kephalaia vocabulary for divine entities subsisting in a realm.

Completes the phrase "within the land that is not revealed" (with "nd" following the bracket), corresponding to the spiritual reading's "interior ground of the will that has not yet been made manifest."

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading states "nothing from the opposition is their equal"; the preceding clause affirms their victory, with "equa" completing to "equals them" — the aeons' endurance against evil is absolute.
The hidden plenitude (divine good) dwells within the Ambassador (divine truth), corresponding to Swedenborg's teaching that divine good resides at the core of divine truth proceeding from the Father.

Standard Kephalaia epithet for a supreme divine light-being; corresponds to the spiritual reading's "divine truth" since in Swedenborg's correspondences, luminary = divine truth made manifest as illuminating light.
Contextually determined by the chapter's subject — the fourteen great aeons of light — corresponding to the spiritual reading's "states of wisdom" in which the Ambassador establishes himself.

The editor's "all" is confirmed: the spiritual reading affirms "all the states of wisdom and all spiritual powers," and the universalizing "all" fits the Ambassador's supreme governing role over the aeons and gods.
Completes the common Kephalaia expression "from the beginning to the end of all things," indicating that divine providence holds the universe together through the entire arc of its existence.
